shots.narration: August 1916. A bare rock at the edge of Antarctica. Twenty-two men are living under two upturned boats.
shots.onScreen: Two wooden boats flipped upside down on a black stone beach, smoke from a chimney hole, glacier behind, snow blowing
shots.motion: slow crane down from the glacier to the hut

shots.narration: Every morning, one man climbs the hill and looks out to sea. His name is Frank Wild.
shots.onScreen: Frank Wild in a ragged parka climbs a snowy ridge and shades his eyes
shots.motion: tracking behind him up the slope
shots.overlay: callout: FRANK WILD / SECOND IN COMMAND

shots.narration: And every morning he tells the others the same thing. Pack your things, boys. The Boss may come today.
shots.onScreen: Wild at the hut doorway, men in sleeping bags looking up, thin and bearded
shots.overlay: quote card: "Lash up and stow, boys. The Boss may come today."

shots.narration: The Boss is Ernest Shackleton. He left in a small open boat four months ago. Nobody knows if he is alive.
shots.onScreen: A tiny lifeboat vanishing into grey waves, seen from the beach
shots.motion: slow pull back from the horizon

shots.narration: This is the story of how twenty-eight men were lost at the bottom of the world for almost two years. And how every one of them came home.
shots.onScreen: The full crew of 28 lined up on the ice beside their ship, then the image freezes and cracks like ice
shots.motion: slow lateral dolly along the line

shots.narration: In 1914, the South Pole had already been reached. Roald Amundsen got there first in 1911.
shots.onScreen: A flag on a snowy pole with a small tent, a sled track leading away

shots.narration: So Ernest Shackleton chose a bigger goal. To walk across the whole of Antarctica, from one sea to the other.
shots.onScreen: Shackleton at a desk with a big map, finger tracing a line across the continent

shots.narration: The plan was to land on the coast of the Weddell Sea, march to the South Pole, and carry on to the Ross Sea. About 2,900 kilometres on foot.
shots.onScreen: Antarctica map; dotted route from Vahsel Bay over the Pole to the Ross Sea; distance counter
shots.motion: map tilt and follow the route line

shots.narration: His ship was called Endurance. A three-masted wooden ship, built to push through ice.
shots.onScreen: Endurance under sail in a grey sea, name on the stern
shots.motion: low angle tracking alongside the hull

shots.narration: On board were twenty-seven men chosen by Shackleton. And one he had turned down.
shots.onScreen: The crew on deck; one young man climbing out of a locker, everyone turning to stare

shots.narration: Perce Blackborow, nineteen years old, had stowed away. Shackleton was furious. He told him that if they ran out of food, he would be the first one eaten.
shots.onScreen: Shackleton facing Blackborow on deck, stern, crew watching
shots.motion: slow push in between the two

shots.narration: Then he signed him on as a steward. The crew was now twenty-eight.
shots.onScreen: Blackborow handed an apron and a pot, a tally on screen ticks up

shots.narration: In November 1914, Endurance reached South Georgia, a whaling island in the South Atlantic. The last human settlement on their route.
shots.onScreen: Map of the South Atlantic, Endurance icon arriving at South Georgia, label Grytviken
shots.motion: map push in to the island

shots.narration: The whalers there gave a warning. The ice in the Weddell Sea was worse that year than anyone could remember.
shots.onScreen: Whalers at a dock with a lantern, pointing south; Shackleton listening

shots.narration: Shackleton waited a month. Then, on the fifth of December 1914, he sailed anyway.
shots.onScreen: Endurance leaving the harbour, snowy peaks behind
shots.motion: wide crane up as the ship leaves

shots.narration: At first the ship pushed through. Then the ice got thicker.
shots.onScreen: Endurance's bow breaking plates of pack ice

shots.narration: On the nineteenth of January 1915, a day's sail from land, the ice closed around Endurance. It was stuck.
shots.onScreen: The ship frozen in a white plain, sails furled
shots.motion: slow crane up to a wide top view

shots.narration: The crew went out with picks, saws and chisels and tried to cut a channel. It did not move an inch.
shots.onScreen: Men hacking at the ice beside the hull, chips flying, the ship unmoved

shots.narration: And now the ice itself began to drift. Taking the ship with it, away from the coast where they had planned to land.
shots.onScreen: Weddell Sea map; ship icon drifting in a slow arc away from Vahsel Bay

shots.narration: Then winter came. In Antarctica that means months without the sun.
shots.onScreen: The sun dips below the horizon and does not return; stars come out over the ship

shots.narration: They lived on board. They played football on the ice, held dog races, and kept each other going.
shots.onScreen: Men kicking a ball on the ice by lantern light; dog teams racing

shots.narration: The ship's photographer, Frank Hurley, took pictures of everything.
shots.onScreen: Hurley behind a box camera on a tripod, flash powder goes off

shots.narration: But the ice was not still. It was pressing in from both sides, and the wooden hull began to groan.
shots.onScreen: Ice ridges rising against the hull, timber flexing
shots.motion: slow push in on the hull

shots.narration: On the twenty-fourth of October 1915, the ice broke through. Water poured into the ship.
shots.onScreen: Inside the hold, water spraying through a split plank

shots.narration: For three days the men pumped, in turns, around the clock. The water rose faster than they could pump it out.
shots.onScreen: Men at a hand pump in the dark, water around their knees

shots.narration: On the twenty-seventh of October, Shackleton gave the order. Abandon ship.
shots.onScreen: Shackleton on deck, lantern raised; men climbing down to the ice with crates
shots.sfx: wind, shout lost in the wind

shots.narration: They had been trapped for nine months. Now they were camped on floating ice, with no radio, no way to call for help, and nobody in the world who knew where they were.
shots.onScreen: Tents on the white ice, the broken ship behind them, tiny under a huge sky
shots.motion: slow pull back into a very wide shot

shots.narration: They had three lifeboats, sledges, some tents and food for a few weeks.
shots.onScreen: The three lifeboats on sledges, supplies stacked, men taking stock

shots.narration: Shackleton told every man to keep only two pounds of personal things. Everything else stayed on the ice.
shots.onScreen: Men emptying bags into a pile in the snow
shots.motion: slow push in on the pile

shots.narration: He went first. He threw away gold coins, and a Bible after tearing out a few pages.
shots.onScreen: Shackleton dropping coins and a book into the snow
shots.motion: close push in on his hands

shots.narration: Hurley had to smash many of his glass negatives. He kept around a hundred and fifty. Those are the photos we have today.
shots.onScreen: Hurley choosing between glass plates, setting some aside, the rest left behind

shots.narration: They tried to drag the boats across the ice towards land. Each boat weighed about a tonne.
shots.onScreen: Men in harness hauling a boat on a sledge through deep soft snow

shots.narration: After three hours of hauling, they had moved about one mile. Shackleton stopped the march.
shots.onScreen: The men look back; the ship still visible close behind them

shots.narration: They set up camp on a big floe and named it Ocean Camp.
shots.onScreen: Tents and a lookout tower on the floe, a sign reading OCEAN CAMP

shots.narration: On the twenty-first of November 1915, the men watched Endurance finally sink. Shackleton said only: She's gone, boys.
shots.onScreen: Far off, the ship's stern lifts and slides under the ice; the men stand silent
shots.motion: slow push in past the men to the ship

shots.narration: In late December they tried another march, and gave up again after a week. The new camp was called Patience Camp.
shots.onScreen: A new set of tents, a sign reading PATIENCE CAMP, men sitting waiting

shots.narration: Food was rationed hard. They hunted seals and penguins, and later had to put down the sledge dogs.
shots.onScreen: Men by a blubber stove, a seal carcass shown only as a dark shape, empty dog kennels
shots.motion: slow push in on the empty kennels

shots.narration: One day a sea leopard chased a man across the ice. Frank Wild shot it. It fed the camp for days.
shots.onScreen: The sea leopard's dark shape lunging from a crack, men running; then a calm aftermath
shots.sfx: splash, running feet, a distant crack

shots.narration: To drink, they packed snow into tins and held them against their bodies to melt it.
shots.onScreen: A man holding a tin inside his coat, a few drops of water

shots.narration: And Shackleton made sure every man had a job. He knew that the real danger was not only cold. It was despair.
shots.onScreen: Men working: mending, cooking, keeping watch

shots.narration: For months the floe drifted north. They hoped it would carry them to Paulet Island, where emergency stores had been left years before.
shots.onScreen: Peninsula map; drift line passing Paulet Island, off to the side
shots.motion: map push in on Paulet Island

shots.narration: On the twenty-third of March 1916, through the fog, they saw land. Joinville Island.
shots.onScreen: Mountains appearing through fog beyond the ice

shots.narration: But it was out of reach, across broken ice. They were drifting past it, towards the open ocean.
shots.onScreen: Map: drift line slides past Joinville and Paulet towards open water

shots.narration: The floe was breaking up around them. On the ninth of April 1916, Shackleton ordered everyone into the three boats.
shots.onScreen: Three boats launched into a lead of black water between floes

shots.narration: That night, the floe they camped on split in two, right under a tent. A sailor named Ernest Holness fell into the sea, still in his sleeping bag.
shots.onScreen: A crack opening under a tent at night, a figure dropping into the black water
shots.motion: slow push in, cut to black water

shots.narration: Shackleton reached down and pulled him out. Then the crack opened wider and Shackleton was left alone on the other piece.
shots.onScreen: Shackleton alone on a small floe drifting into the dark, the others on the far side

shots.narration: The men pushed out a boat and brought him back. Then Shackleton made Holness walk all night, so he would not freeze in his wet clothes.
shots.onScreen: Holness walking in circles by lantern light, steam rising from his clothes

shots.narration: For almost a week they rowed and sailed between the floes, soaked and freezing, with almost nothing to drink.
shots.onScreen: The three boats in a grey sea between ice, men hunched over oars

shots.narration: On the fifteenth of April 1916, they landed on Elephant Island. It was the first solid ground they had stood on for 497 days.
shots.onScreen: A boat grinding onto a stone beach; men stumbling ashore, one kneeling and touching the stones
shots.motion: low angle on the beach as they step out

shots.narration: But nobody would ever look for them here. Elephant Island was empty, far from any shipping route.
shots.onScreen: Wide view of the island: black cliffs, glaciers, nothing else
shots.motion: slow pull back to a very wide shot

shots.narration: The nearest people were at the whaling stations on South Georgia. 1,300 kilometres away, across the Southern Ocean.
shots.onScreen: Map: dotted line from Elephant Island to South Georgia, distance counter

shots.narration: Shackleton decided to go for help in the biggest lifeboat, the James Caird, about seven metres long.
shots.onScreen: The James Caird on the beach, men raising its sides and fitting a canvas deck

shots.narration: He took five men with him. Frank Worsley to navigate, Tom Crean, the carpenter Harry McNish, and two sailors, Timothy McCarthy and John Vincent.
shots.onScreen: Six men lined up by the boat, name callouts one by one
shots.overlay: callouts: WORSLEY · CREAN · McNISH · McCARTHY · VINCENT

shots.narration: On the twenty-fourth of April 1916, they pushed off. Twenty-two men watched them go.
shots.onScreen: The boat leaving the beach, men on the shore waving
shots.motion: crane up from the shore to the open sea

shots.narration: They sailed through one of the roughest seas on Earth, in waves as tall as buildings.
shots.onScreen: The tiny boat climbing a huge grey wave
shots.motion: low angle as the wave rises

shots.narration: They took turns, four hours at the helm, four hours trying to sleep in a soaking space under the canvas.
shots.onScreen: Two men at the tiller in spray; others curled under the deck

shots.narration: Worsley found their way with a sextant, catching the sun when it showed for a few seconds through the clouds.
shots.onScreen: Worsley bracing in the boat, sextant raised to a pale sun

shots.narration: Ice formed on the boat and made it top-heavy. They had to crawl out and chip it off before it rolled them over.
shots.onScreen: Men on the icy canvas chipping ice with axes, the boat leaning

shots.narration: After sixteen days, they saw South Georgia. Then a hurricane hit, and nearly threw them onto the rocks.
shots.onScreen: Cliffs through storm spray; the boat pitching close to the rocks

shots.narration: On the tenth of May 1916, they landed in King Haakon Bay. They had made it.
shots.onScreen: The boat grinding onto a small beach in a cove, men collapsing on the stones

shots.narration: But they had landed on the wrong side of the island. The whaling station at Stromness was on the other side, across the mountains.
shots.onScreen: South Georgia map; landing point and Stromness on opposite coasts, mountains between

shots.narration: The boat was too damaged to sail around. Nobody had ever crossed the island's mountains on foot.
shots.onScreen: The battered James Caird on the beach; jagged snowy peaks behind
shots.motion: slow tilt up from the boat to the peaks

shots.narration: They rested and ate for nine days. Then, on the nineteenth of May, Shackleton, Worsley and Crean set off. Three men stayed with the boat.
shots.onScreen: Three men walking away from the cove at night with a rope and an adze

shots.narration: McNish had pulled screws from the boat and fixed them into their boots for grip. They carried no tents and no sleeping bags.
shots.onScreen: Close on boots with screws poking out of the soles

shots.narration: Again and again they climbed a ridge, found a sheer drop on the other side, and had to turn back.
shots.onScreen: Three tiny figures on a ridge edge, a cliff below them
shots.motion: slow crane past them to the drop

shots.narration: Night was falling on a high ridge. If they stayed, they would freeze. So they coiled the rope into sledges, sat down, and slid down the mountain in the dark.
shots.onScreen: The three men sitting in a line on a coiled rope sliding down a long snow slope

shots.narration: At seven in the morning, they heard a steam whistle. The whalers at Stromness were being called to work.
shots.onScreen: The three men stopping on a ridge, a faint whistle ring graphic

shots.narration: On the twentieth of May 1916, after thirty-six hours of walking, three men with black faces and long beards walked into the whaling station.
shots.onScreen: Three ragged men walking past whale-oil tanks; workers staring

shots.narration: The station manager knew Shackleton well. He did not recognise him. Then Shackleton said his name.
shots.onScreen: The manager at his door staring at the three strangers; recognition on his face
shots.motion: slow push in on the manager

shots.narration: Nobody crossed South Georgia on foot again until 1955, and those were trained mountaineers with full equipment.
shots.onScreen: The island's mountains from above, a dotted route over them

shots.narration: That night, a whaling boat went round to King Haakon Bay and picked up the other three men.
shots.onScreen: A small steam boat entering the cove, three men waving on the beach

shots.narration: Now Shackleton had to get back to Elephant Island. Twenty-two men were still waiting.
shots.onScreen: Shackleton on a ship's bridge looking south, worried

shots.narration: He tried three times, in three different ships. Each time, the pack ice turned him back.
shots.onScreen: Three ship icons approaching a wall of ice and turning away one after another

shots.narration: On Elephant Island, the men lived under the two upturned boats. Wild kept them busy and kept them believing.
shots.onScreen: Inside the dark boat-hut, men crowded around a blubber stove

shots.narration: Blackborow, the stowaway, had frostbite in his feet. The two surgeons had to remove the toes of his left foot, by the light of the stove.
shots.onScreen: The hut interior, two surgeons by the stove, Blackborow lying under blankets; only their faces shown
shots.motion: slow push in on the surgeons' faces

shots.narration: Weeks turned into months. Some of the men started to believe the Boss was dead.
shots.onScreen: Snow piling around the hut, a tally of days scratched on a board

shots.narration: Wild began planning to sail one of the last boats to Deception Island himself.
shots.onScreen: Wild studying a hand-drawn map by the stove

shots.narration: Then, on the thirtieth of August 1916, a ship came round the point. A small Chilean steam tug called the Yelcho.
shots.onScreen: A small steamer appears through the haze off the island; the men run out of the hut
shots.motion: wide, slow push in on the ship

shots.narration: Shackleton stood in the boat as it came in, counting the figures on the beach. Two, five, seven. All twenty-two.
shots.onScreen: Shackleton standing in a rowing boat, the men on the shore; a counter ticks to 22
shots.motion: over Shackleton's shoulder to the beach

shots.narration: In under an hour, every man was on board.
shots.onScreen: The men climbing aboard the Yelcho, the boat-hut left behind on the empty beach
shots.motion: crane up as the ship leaves

shots.narration: All twenty-eight men of the Endurance came home. On the other side of Antarctica, the expedition's Ross Sea party was not so lucky. Three of them died.
shots.onScreen: The 28 lined up again, warm light; then a small memorial card for the Ross Sea party
shots.motion: slow lateral dolly, then hold on the card

shots.narration: In 2022, explorers found Endurance three kilometres down on the floor of the Weddell Sea. Its name is still on the stern.
shots.onScreen: A deep-sea robot's light sweeps over a wooden stern; the name ENDURANCE in gold letters
shots.motion: slow push in through dark water

shots.narration: Shackleton failed to cross Antarctica. But he brought every one of his men home alive. Today he is buried on South Georgia, where the journey began.
shots.onScreen: A grave with a granite headstone on a green hillside above the bay; end title
shots.motion: slow crane up from the grave to the bay
